key_insight: The paper makes real-time robust optimal control tractable for nonlinear and neural-network dynamics by combining tight, differentiable linearization error bounds with GPU-parallel LTV-based planning.
engineering_relevance: This enables formally verified, online safety-critical control policies with tighter reachable tubes and lower conservativeness for high-dimensional systems.
method: Path-based Hessian bounds for analytic dynamics produce tighter linearization error bounds than standard interval methods.
Certified bounds for neural-network dynamics use verifier-generated affine relaxations plus local Jacobian corrections.
The GPU-parallel robust control solver is extended to handle right-invertible disturbance matrices and non-zero-centered zonotopic uncertainty sets.
evidence_signal: On nonlinear and neural-network systems up to 168 state dimensions, the method reportedly achieves up to 67 Hz while reducing solve time and conservativeness relative to baselines.
watch_item: Performance and tightness depend on the quality of the certified bounds and solver extensions, which may be harder to maintain for very complex models or when verifier assumptions are restrictive.
paper_title: GPU-Parallel Linearization Error Bounds for Real-Time Robust Optimal Control of Nonlinear and Neural Network Dynamics
